description: A stochastic oscillator in the manner of Xenakis: the wave is a run of line segments whose end points wander at random from one cycle to the next

params.text: Sets the pitch, 0 giving C0 at 16.35Hz and each whole step up an octave, over a range of six octaves
Sets how far the timing of each segment's end point is allowed to wander from cycle to cycle, none at the far left
Sets how far the height of each segment's end point is allowed to wander from cycle to cycle, none at the far left
Pulls the wandering of the timings back towards the reference wave, so the pitch stays put instead of drifting
Pulls the wandering of the heights back towards the reference wave, so the shape stays close to it
Sets how many line segments make up one cycle, 3 to 64
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the time randomness CV
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, on the amplitude randomness CV
Puts every segment back on the reference wave
Throws fresh random values into every segment at once

inputs.text: Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, added to the pitch knob; the number of channels here sets the polyphony of the whole module
Adds to the time randomness knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of its travel at full attenuation
Adds to the amplitude randomness knob through its attenuverter, a volt covering a tenth of its travel at full attenuation
Adds to the destruct pitch knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel, with no attenuator
Adds to the destruct shape knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel, with no attenuator
A rising edge past 2V puts every segment back on the reference wave
A rising edge past 2V throws fresh random values into every segment

outputs.text: The first of the two waves, up to 5V either way
The second of the two waves, up to 5V either way; it is a separate oscillator with its own random walk, and it is only computed while a cable is in it

notes: with both randomness knobs at zero the module puts out the reference wave unchanged, so it makes no sound of its own until one of them is raised
the two outputs are two independent runs of the same process, not a stereo pair, although the maker's tooltips call them left and right
menu: Quantize pitch knob: Continuous, Semitones, Octaves — snaps the pitch knob only, leaving the V/oct input unquantised
Reference wave form: Sine, Zero — sets the shape the segments are pulled back towards by the two destruct controls

inputs.0:
1V per octave · continuous · polyphonic

inputs.5:

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
